approach: Write v as a constant times t to the power three-quarters, then integrate for displacement and differentiate for acceleration.

steps.text: Write the velocity as a constant times t raised to the power three-quarters.
Integrate v with respect to time to get the displacement.
Differentiate v with respect to time to get the acceleration.
So displacement grows as t to the power seven-quarters, and acceleration falls as t to the power minus one-quarter.

common_mistakes.text: Differentiating t to the power three-quarters by only multiplying by three-quarters and keeping the same power gives an acceleration wrongly stated as proportional to t^(3/4) instead of t^(−1/4).
